source.name: Sunako's 4chan Fuuka Archiver
source.short-desc: Sunako's Fuuka-based 4chan archive, media and database, around 2015-10-20
source.capture:
1.8TB item of which ONE 5.1GB file is post data: sunakos-fuuka-sql_somewhat-corrupt.tar.gz. Everything else is media — 50 tarballs, the largest being sunako-g-media-2015-10-20.tar.gz at 301.5GB. Surveyed against archive.org/metadata (55 files).

THE PAYLOAD IS NAMED 'somewhat-corrupt' BY THE UPLOADER. That is not a guess about it, it is the filename — and it is the ONLY evidence available, because the IA item has no description whatsoever (checked: metadata.description is absent, and the only other fields are scanner/uploader/curation boilerplate). Nothing states what is corrupt, how much, or which boards. That has to be established after unpacking, and it is the first thing to do with this source rather than an afterthought.

Treat the dump as damaged until proven otherwise: expect truncated statements, and expect an adapter to abort part-way rather than fail at the start. ingest-all records completion only on a clean adapter return, so a run that dies deep into this file will correctly leave it unmarked — but the rows written before the abort stay, which is fine (the UNIQUE constraint makes a re-run idempotent) as long as nobody reads 'has rows' as 'finished'. Compare against archive_ten_billion_patched, where the corruption was one known byte at a known offset with a documented fix; here there is no such information, so the extent must be measured rather than looked up.

BOARD COVERAGE, inferred from the media tarball names since the SQL is a single opaque archive: g (301.5GB of media), m, jp, c, w, h, e, u, a, plus a/image/ split into numbered volumes. /g/ media dominating by a wide margin suggests /g/ is a major part of the text too, which would make this relevant to the /g/ gap — but the board list inside the SQL tarball is UNVERIFIED and the media names are only circumstantial.

DATE: media files are stamped 2015-10-20 and the item was added 2016-05-24, so this is a 2015-era snapshot. It does not reach the post-2017 /g/ gap.

EXCLUDE PATTERNS must cover FOUR spellings, which this item uses inconsistently: `-media-` (the large per-board tarballs), `-images-`, `-thumbs-` (a separate 16GB set that is easy to overlook because every entry is small next to the 301GB media files), and the nested a/image/ numbered volumes. Verified with --dry-run: 55 files / 1.8TB reduces to 5 files / 5.1GB. A leaky pattern is expensive here in a way it is not elsewhere — omitting the thumbs rule alone pulled an extra 11GB.

ADAPTER NULL DELIBERATELY. 'Fuuka' in the name says nothing reliable: laza-4chan-archive is also called Fuuka and is really Asagi (`thread_num`), while installgentoo-net is true Fuuka (`parent`) and needed warosu-sql. Both adapters silently accept zero tables on a schema mismatch instead of erroring, so the schema must be read from the CREATE TABLE after unpacking, not assumed from the archiver's name.

prepare.name: stage the .sql dumps for ingest
prepare.run: mkdir -p out && find extracted -name '*.sql' -exec sh -c 'cp -al "$1" out/ 2>/dev/null || cp -a "$1" out/' _ {} ';'
